To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

community attitudes towards asylum seekers were influenced by the perceived threats that asylum seekers posed to traditional Australian values and that the way these threats were reinforced in media and political discourse.

The Australian community is generally positive towards refugees and asylum seekers, and is generally opposed to mandatory detention and the use of offshore processing centres, but that the Australian public is generally not well informed about the issues surrounding the arrival of asylum seeker by boat and the Australian government's policies towards this group of immigrants.

the community perceptions and attitudes towards asylum seekers were influenced by a complex mix of personal experiences, traditional Australian values, media and political rhetoric, and the way in which these values and norms were threatened by asylum seekers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the way that asylum seekers are portrayed and perceived in the media and how this impacts upon community attitudes and perceptions of asylum seekers.
the role of community attitudes in shaping the social and political context in which asylum seekers live in Australia.

the way that community perceptions and attitudes are influenced by a range of factors, including personal contact with asylum seeking immigrants, the threat that these immigrants pose to traditional values and norms, and the role played by media and political rhetoric in shaping community perceptions and attitudes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the majority of respondents in our study held negative attitudes toward asylum seekers and that these attitudes were shaped by the interplay of traditional Australian norms, media, and political rhetoric.
the Australian public is generally supportive of the humanitarian program, but not of asylum seekers who come through irregular channels.
community attitudes and perceptions towards asylum seekers were not necessarily negative but were strongly influenced by media and political rhetoric.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the majority of the Australian community would welcome asylum seekers if they were to arrive by 'the proper channel' and not by boat.
the Australian community is largely supportive of the humanitarian program but is less supportive of the asylum seeker arrivals by boat.
community perceptions and attitudes are shaped more by the way that asylum seekers are presented in the media and by political rhetoric than by direct personal contact with this group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Australian public is not opposed to the arrival of asylum seeking immigrants per se.

while the majority of respondents were sympathetic to the plight of asylum seekers, many felt that the government was not doing enough to protect the Australian community and that the government was too lenient in allowing asylum seekers to enter the country.

while the majority of respondents in our sample were not opposed to Australia's resettlement programme and were not opposed to the arrival of asylum seeker boats, they felt strongly that the government should be doing more to prevent the boats arriving in the first place.
